title: JavaScript `this`, Prototypes and Classes: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of how `this` is bound in JavaScript (default, implicit, explicit, new, arrow), call/apply/bind, the prototype chain, and classes as syntactic sugar over prototypes.

chapters.title: The this Mental Model
points: Definition: `this` is decided by HOW a function is called (call-site), not where it is defined; arrow functions are the exception
Binding priority, highest first: new > explicit (call/apply/bind) > implicit (obj.fn()) > default
Default binding: plain `fn()` gives `this = globalThis` in sloppy mode and `undefined` in strict mode (modules and classes are always strict)
Implicit binding: `obj.fn()` sets `this = obj`, only the object immediately left of the dot counts (`a.b.fn()` gives `b`)
Comparison: the four call-site rules plus arrow lexical `this` in one view, with the question to ask at each call: new? call/apply/bind? obj.? plain?

chapters.title: Explicit, new and Arrow Binding
points: `fn.call(ctx, a, b)` runs immediately with `this = ctx` and args passed one by one; `fn.apply(ctx, [a, b])` takes an args array
`fn.bind(ctx, a)` returns a NEW function with `this` permanently fixed (plus partial args); it does not run; a second bind or call cannot change it
`new Fn()` steps: create an empty object linked to `Fn.prototype`, run `Fn` with `this` = that object, return it unless `Fn` returns another object
Arrow functions have no own `this`, `arguments` or `prototype`; they capture `this` lexically from the enclosing scope, so call/apply/bind cannot rebind them and `new` throws
Example: `setTimeout(obj.method, 0)` loses `this`; fix with `obj.method.bind(obj)` or `() => obj.method()`

chapters.title: Prototype Chain Internals
points: Every object has an internal [[Prototype]] (read via `Object.getPrototypeOf(o)`); property lookup walks o, then its prototype, up to `Object.prototype`, then `null` (gives `undefined`)

`Fn.prototype` is the object assigned as [[Prototype]] of instances made with `new Fn()`; `obj.__proto__` is the legacy accessor to the same link, so `Object.getPrototypeOf(new Fn()) === Fn.prototype`
Writes go on the object itself and shadow the prototype property; reads fall through the chain
`Object.create(proto)` makes an object with the given prototype; `Object.create(null)` makes a dictionary object with no chain
Check with `obj.hasOwnProperty(k)` or `Object.hasOwn(obj, k)` (own only) versus `k in obj` (own plus inherited) versus `a instanceof Fn` (is `Fn.prototype` in a's chain)

chapters.title: Classes as Sugar over Prototypes
points: `class A { m() {} }` puts `m` on `A.prototype` (shared, non-enumerable); `constructor` is the function body; `typeof A === 'function'`
`extends` sets `B.prototype`'s [[Prototype]] to `A.prototype` and `B`'s own [[Prototype]] to `A`, so static methods inherit too
In a derived constructor, `super(...)` must run before touching `this`, otherwise a ReferenceError is thrown
Differences from plain functions: calling a class without `new` throws TypeError, class bodies are strict, and declarations are in the temporal dead zone (not hoisted usably)
Class field arrow `handle = () => {...}` creates a per-instance bound method (own property, not on the prototype), the usual fix for lost `this` in callbacks

chapters.title: Common this Mistakes
points: Extracting a method, `const f = obj.method; f()`, loses implicit binding and falls to default (`undefined` in strict mode, so a TypeError on property access)
Arrow function as an object-literal method: `{ name: 'x', hi: () => this.name }` takes `this` from the outer scope, not the object
Regular `function` callback inside a method (`arr.forEach(function(){ this... })`) gets default binding; use an arrow function or pass `thisArg`
`bind` returns a new function each time, so `addEventListener('click', fn.bind(o))` cannot be removed later; keep a reference
Forgetting `new` on a constructor function sets properties on the global object in sloppy mode; mutating `Fn.prototype` objects shares state across all instances

chapters.title: this and Prototypes Cheat Sheet
points: Resolve `this` in order: new, then call/apply/bind, then `obj.fn()`, then default (`undefined` strict), with arrows ignoring all of these and using the enclosing `this`
`call(ctx, a, b)` runs now with listed args; `apply(ctx, [a, b])` runs now with an array; `bind(ctx, a)` returns a function to run later
Lookup: own property, then `[[Prototype]]` chain, then `undefined`; `Object.getPrototypeOf`, `Object.create`, `Object.hasOwn`, `in`, `instanceof`
Class = constructor function plus methods on `.prototype`; `extends` links both prototype and static chain; `super()` before `this`
Callback losing `this` fix list: arrow function, `.bind(obj)`, class field arrow, or `const self = this`
